sections.h2: When does a South Carolina estate need probate?
sections.html:
A will in South Carolina has to be validated by an order of informal probate or an adjudication of probate before it can prove a transfer of property or name a personal representative (SC Code 62-3-102). The main exception is the small estate affidavit, covered below. If a house sits in the decedent's name alone, the family usually needs a court-appointed personal representative before anyone can sign a deed.

There is also an outer limit. No informal, formal testacy or appointment proceeding may start more than ten years after the death, with a short list of exceptions (62-3-108). After that, intestacy is treated as incontestable if nothing was filed.

sections.h2: Who is allowed to act as personal representative?
sections.html:
South Carolina ranks who gets first call on the appointment, and the person named in the will comes first. Under 62-3-203 the order runs like this:

  1. The person with priority under a probated will, including a nominee named in it
  2. A surviving spouse who is also a devisee
  3. Other devisees
  4. A surviving spouse
  5. Other heirs
  6. A creditor, starting 45 days after death, if the creditor follows 62-3-804(1)(b)
  7. The South Carolina Department of Revenue or a suitable person the court picks, starting four months after death

Anyone under eighteen is disqualified. Siblings who disagree about who should serve are a common reason a house sits unsold for months, so settle that early.

sections.h2: What is the difference between informal and formal probate?
sections.html:
Informal probate starts with a verified application to the court; formal testacy is a litigated proceeding started by a summons and petition. The informal application must state the applicant's interest, the decedent's name, date of death, age and domicile, and the names and addresses of the spouse, children, heirs and devisees (62-3-301). It must also say the ten-year limit has not run.

Formal testacy exists to decide whether a valid will was left (62-3-401). While one is pending, the court may not act on informal probate or appointment applications. A contest of an informally probated will may be brought within eight months of informal probate or one year of death, whichever is later (62-3-108(A)(2)(c)). A buyer or title company will care about that window.

sections.h2: What deadlines apply after the personal representative is appointed?
sections.html:
Several clocks start at appointment, and a few start at death. Here are the ones in the probate article:

StepDeadlineSection
Notice of appointment to heirs and deviseesWithin 30 days of appointment62-3-705
Inventory and appraisementWithin 90 days of appointment62-3-704(b), 62-3-706(A)
Creditor claims after published noticeEight months after first publication62-3-801(a)
Outer limit for claims arising before deathOne year after death62-3-803(a)
Pay allowed claims before closingNo later than 14 months after death, absent an extension62-3-807(a)

These clocks decide when a family can safely distribute proceeds, which is a separate question from when the house can be sold.

sections.h2: Can a personal representative sell the house?
sections.html:
Yes, the statute lets a personal representative acquire or dispose of an asset, including land, for cash or on credit, at public or private sale (62-3-715). That power begins on appointment (62-3-701), so a sale contract signed before the court issues letters is on shaky ground.

At closing, the title company will want to see the letters, and a South Carolina deed from the estate is typically signed by the personal representative. Once the estate distributes real property instead of selling it, the personal representative must execute a deed of distribution to evidence the distributee's title (62-3-907(A)). Heirs who inherit and then want out can sell afterward, but that adds a recording step.

Bond can matter too. Bond may be waived by affidavit when the estate's gross value is under twenty thousand dollars (62-3-603(B)(1)), and an interested person or creditor with a claim over five thousand dollars may demand one (62-3-605). Ask the probate court how it handles bond in your county.

sections.h2: What does the $45,000 small estate rule cover?
sections.html:
South Carolina lets a successor collect personal property by affidavit when the whole probate estate, less liens and encumbrances, is worth no more than $45,000 (62-3-1201(a)). Real estate is the catch, and the section governs collection of personal property, so a house usually needs a personal representative anyway.

  • At least 30 days must have passed since death.
  • No application or petition for a personal representative may be pending or granted anywhere.
  • The probate judge of the decedent's county of domicile must approve and countersign the affidavit.
  • The affidavit is filed in that county's probate court.

A related summary route lets a personal representative close an estate not over $45,000 by sworn statement (62-3-1203, 62-3-1204), and the appointment ends one year after death if no claims or proceedings are pending.

sections.h2: How are creditors paid when the estate is short?
sections.html:
When assets run short, South Carolina pays claims in a set order (62-3-805). That matters if the house must be sold to cover debts.

  • Costs of administration, including attorney's fees and reasonable funeral expenses
  • Debts and taxes with preference under federal law
  • Reasonable medical, hospital and personal care costs of the last illness
  • Debts and taxes with preference under South Carolina law
  • All other claims

The personal representative must publish the creditor notice once a week for three successive weeks in a county newspaper (62-3-801(a)). A claim not presented in time is barred.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell an inherited house in South Carolina?
sections.html:
Most inherited-house sales in South Carolina slow down at the same few points: getting letters issued, finding the original will, agreeing among heirs, and clearing back property tax or liens. South Carolina has 46 counties, so local habits and timing vary. Call the probate court in the county where the decedent lived before you plan around a date.

Cash Home Buyers works with personal representatives and heirs who want to sell the house as-is. We can talk before appointment, but a closing needs authority to sign. Bring the death certificate, the will if there is one, and any court paperwork you already have.

sections.h2: What does a personal representative owe the heirs?
sections.html:
A personal representative is a fiduciary who must settle and distribute the estate under the will and the Code, as expeditiously as is consistent with the estate's best interests (62-3-703(a)). That duty applies to a house just as it does to bank accounts. Delay that costs the estate money, such as months of carrying costs on a vacant property, is the kind of thing heirs can question.

The personal representative also has the same standing to sue and be sued as the decedent had before death, except for proceedings that do not survive death (62-3-703(c)). The first person issued general letters has exclusive authority until that appointment ends or is modified (62-3-702). Acts that benefited the estate before appointment can relate back, and the personal representative may ratify acts others did for the estate (62-3-701).

sections.h2: Is there a faster path when one heir inherits everything?
sections.html:
Yes, a narrower one. If the appointed personal representative is the sole devisee or sole heir, that person may distribute the estate immediately after publishing the creditor notice and then file a closing statement (62-3-1203(b)). The closing statement is a verified document stating the estate was fully administered and distributed, and that a copy went to distributees and known unpaid creditors (62-3-1204(a)).

Under 62-3-301(a)(7) the court may also probate a will without appointing a personal representative. Whether that helps with a house sale depends on the title company, so ask before you list or sign anything.

sections.h2: What documents do you need to gather first?
sections.html:
Most delays come from missing paperwork. Start with this list:

  • A certified death certificate
  • The original will, if one exists, since the application must say whether the original is with the court or attached (62-3-402(a))
  • Names and addresses of the spouse, children, heirs and devisees, with ages for minors (62-3-301)
  • The current deed and a recent property tax bill
  • Mortgage statements and any lien notices

If the original will is lost, the petition must state its contents and say it is lost, destroyed or otherwise unavailable (62-3-402(a)).

faqs.q: Do I need probate to sell a house in South Carolina?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if the house is titled only in the decedent's name. The will must be validated under 62-3-102, and a personal representative then has power to sell land under 62-3-715. Confirm your facts with the probate court.

faqs.q: How long does South Carolina probate take?
faqs.a: There is no single timeline. The statute sets deadlines such as 30 days for notice to heirs, 90 days for the inventory, and eight months for creditor claims after publication. Allowed claims should be paid by 14 months after death unless extended.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell the house without a personal representative?
faqs.a: Generally not. A deed from the estate needs someone with authority. The small estate affidavit in 62-3-1201 collects personal property and does not by itself authorize a deed to land.

faqs.q: What is a deed of distribution?
faqs.a: It is the deed a personal representative signs to pass real property to a distributee, and it serves as evidence of that person's title (62-3-907(A)).

faqs.q: Can someone contest the will after informal probate?
faqs.a: Yes. A contest may be started within eight months of informal probate or one year of death, whichever is later (62-3-108(A)(2)(c)).
